statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope -3 in the x direction and slope -4 in the y direction.
(a) A change of -0.2 in x and 0.1 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=6 when x=2 and y=4, what is the value of z when x=2 and y=4.2?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope -3 in the x direction, and slope -4 in the y direction, we have: z = -3 x - 4 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (-3 (x + \Delta x) - 4(y + \Delta y) + c) - (-3 x - 4 y + c) = -3 \Delta x - 4 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = -0.2 and \Delta y = 0.1, we have \Delta z = -3 (-0.2) - 4(0.1) = 0.2. So a -0.2 change in x and a 0.1 change in y produces a 0.2 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=6 when x=2 and y=4, the value of z when x=2 and y=4.2 will be z = 6 + \Delta z = 6 - 3\Delta x - 4\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 2 to 2 and y changes from 4 to 4.2. We have \Delta x = 2 - 2 = 5.55111512312578e-17 and \Delta y = 4.2 - 4 = 0.2. Therefore, when x=2 and y=4.2, we have z = 6 - 3 \cdot(5.55111512312578e-17) - 4\cdot(0.2) = 5.2.
